title: Document
description: Canonical published document revision produced by document-intelligence.

document_revision.description: Published revision for this logical document.

processing_manifest_id.description: Immutable DI processing result that produced this revision.

primary_artifact_id.description: Primary artifact selected as the canonical anchor for this revision.

jurisdiction_id.description: Resolved or source-default jurisdiction reference when available.

authority_id.description: Resolved or source-default authority reference when available.

level.description: Rank in the hierarchy of norms (ADR-0033). NORMALLY OMITTED: the projection derives the level from the document's jurisdiction, which is the honest source — the jurisdiction already knows whether it is a commune, a canton or the Confederation. Declare it only for `constitutional`, the one level the jurisdiction cannot supply (the BV is enacted by the same federal jurisdiction as an ordinary statute). A declared level that would rank the norm BELOW its jurisdiction is ignored. See contracts/vocabularies/norm-level.json.

in_force_from.description: First date the norm was in force. Defaults to `effective_date` at projection time, so producers only set this when entry into force differs from the effective date.

in_force_until.description: Last date the norm WAS in force — INCLUSIVE. Repeal / end of validity. Without it, 'was this in force on 2019-06-01?' is unanswerable, so a `lifecycle_status` of `repealed` with no date here resolves to `unknown` rather than being guessed either way (ADR-0033). PRODUCER OBLIGATION (#843): upstream sources publish BOTH conventions and the field name never tells you which — a producer whose source publishes the first day OUT of force must subtract one day before emitting this. Measured 2026-09-03: AT RIS `Ausserkrafttretensdatum` and Fedlex `jolux:dateEndApplicability` are inclusive (pass through); LexFind `version_inactive_since` is exclusive (converted in `lexfind_api_provider.temporal_metadata`). Getting this wrong by one day reports a repealed norm as good law on its repeal date, because the consumer repeals only on `asOf > in_force_until`.

delegates_to.description: Competence this norm hands DOWN — e.g. a cantonal Hundegesetz delegating to communes the power to regulate dogs. NOT derivable from the jurisdiction tree: it is an assertion made BY the norm's text, so it requires extraction or curation. UNPOPULATED TODAY; the shape is declared so the edge has a home and producers have a target. `subordinate_to` (which norms outrank this one) IS derived and lives on the search projection, not here — subordination is a fact about the tree, delegation is a fact about the text.

target_level.description: Level the competence is delegated TO.

target_jurisdiction_id.description: Specific jurisdiction the competence is delegated to, when the norm names one.

section_id.description: Section of THIS document that makes the delegation — the provision an agent must cite when arguing the commune was authorised.

scope.description: Subject matter of the delegated competence, as stated by the norm.

processing_version.description: DI pipeline version that produced this revision.

lifecycle_status.description: Lifecycle state of the published document revision.

body_text.description: Normalized body text used for sectionization and indexing.

official_citation.description: Canonical official publication citation when one can be derived reliably.

regeste.description: The official headnote the source itself published for a decision, verbatim — the Swiss `Regeste`, the Austrian `Rechtssatz`/`Leitsatz`/`Stammrechtssatz`. Promoted by the pipeline from an explicit normalizer field or from `extracted_metadata.headnote`; never synthesised from the body and never taken from a generated summary, because a fabricated headnote is indistinguishable from an official one once indexed. Absent when the source published none — which is the normal case for statutes and ordinances.

original_language.description: Original source language when the pipeline can determine it reliably.

translation_status.description: Translation state of the published content.

eli_uri.description: European Legislation Identifier URI for this document revision when available. Carries the FRBR identity (Work/Expression/Manifestation) round-trippable with Fedlex, Légifrance, EUR-Lex, and other ELI-publishing systems. See docs/architecture/vocabulary-standards.md.

celex.description: EU CELEX identifier when this document is an EU legal act. Carried alongside eli_uri for EU documents; the citation extractor already recognises this shape.

subdivision.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code when the document's jurisdiction is sub-federal (cantonal, Land, régional, regione). See contracts/vocabularies/subdivisions.json for the registry.

extensions.description: Non-canonical extension area for experimental fields.
